detailed_description: Live-action 1970s Shaw Brothers historical studio cinema, ancient Troy, saturated 35mm film colors, theatrical hard light, practical timber and stone sets. One enormous hollow wooden Trojan horse, visibly made from timber planks with the same golden bronze bands, mounted on the same four-wheeled timber platform. Its four rigid wooden legs never walk, its head never moves, and its wheels rotate only while pulled. One rectangular hinged hatch on its camera-facing belly and one wooden ladder. The Greek leader is the bearded short-dark-haired man in engraved bronze armor and a red cloak, with one sword sheathed at his right hip and no shield. His companion is the clean-shaven curly-dark-haired man in engraved bronze armor and a blue cloak, with one sword sheathed at his right hip and one round bronze shield strapped to his back. They use free hands to climb. Keep faces, hair, armor, cloak colors, equipment ownership and horse construction consistent. [Shot 1] Sunset. New wide shot of the central square. The wooden horse rolls its last small distance and comes to a complete stop beside the stone fountain between two bronze braziers. The Trojan workers release the ropes and walk away. The wooden body remains rigid, hatch completely shut. All Greek soldiers are concealed and invisible. Hold the final parked position with a slow push-in. overall_soundscape: Wheels slow and stop, footsteps recede, fountain water and evening wind. No dialogue or music. non_diegetic_music: None.
